value.first: For the 3am wakings I'd use the Ferber method, also called graduated check-ins. It's one of the best-studied sleep methods there is, and it works at 3am because falling asleep alone at bedtime is the same skill he needs to go back down at night. Start on a night that opens a clear week. Keep the same bedtime and 20-30 minute routine, with the feed before the book. Then put him in the crib drowsy but awake, say goodnight, and leave.
value.second: Nights 1-3: when he cries, at bedtime or at 3am, wait before going in. Night 1: 3, then 5, then 10 minutes, and 10 for every check after. Night 2: 5, 10, 12. Night 3: 10, 12, 15. At 3am, restart that night's sequence from the first wait. Checks last 1-2 minutes: lights off, calm voice, the same short phrase, then leave even mid-cry. No pickup, no feed. Expect night 2 or 3 to be worse. That's the old pattern breaking.
value.third: Nights 4-7: keep stretching the waits, up to 20, 25, 30 by night 7. Working looks like shorter protests and him settling in minutes. If you can't do the waiting, the chair method is the gentler, slower version. If he snores, gasps or pauses in his breathing while asleep, that's worth a doctor's look. I'll check in Thursday.
